subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: What should OpenClaw promise when Dashboard `/compact` or pre-turn recovery encounters an ordinary `claude-cli` session whose native transcript is already at or over the context cap?
rationale: Current source intentionally defers ordinary Claude CLI compaction to the native backend, while the issue asks for stronger OpenClaw-owned recovery or refusal behavior; choosing that contract affects runtime ownership, Dashboard UX, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Fail Loudly With Recovery Guidance
options.body: Keep Claude CLI native ownership, but make OpenClaw detect the unsupported over-cap state and surface clear export/manual-prune/restart guidance without rotating away context.

options.title: Add OpenClaw Fallback Summarization
options.body: Implement and live-test a bounded fallback that reads the Claude CLI transcript and summarizes with a safe alternate path when native compaction cannot proceed.

options.title: Trust Native Claude Compaction
options.body: Close the OpenClaw recovery gap only if live proof shows Claude Code preserves context across this over-cap path and Dashboard copy makes that ownership explicit.

recommendation.title: Fail Loudly With Recovery Guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Claude CLI native ownership, but make OpenClaw detect the unsupported over-cap state and surface clear export/manual-prune/restart guidance without rotating away context.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest recent history match across the compaction, gateway session, and chat UI surfaces that need the product decision.
